title: Foundation — Running Prehab
subtitle: Bodyweight strength base for runners
coaching_note: This isn't a substitute for running, it's what keeps you running injury-free while your mileage builds. Single-leg strength and hip stability are what most runners skip — that's exactly why this session exists.

exercises.name: Leg Swings (front-back and side-to-side)
exercises.form_cue: Hold a wall for balance, controlled swing through a full range.
exercises.why: Opens the hips through the exact planes running demands, before you load them.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.form_cue: Drive through your heels, squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
exercises.why: Wakes up the glutes that a desk job or long runs at low effort can leave under-recruited.

phases.name: Single-Leg Strength
phases.coaching_note: Running is a single-leg sport — every stride lands on one foot. This block is where the injury prevention actually happens.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
exercises.form_cue: One foot flat, other leg extended straight out. Drive through the planted heel, keep your hips level — don't let the free side drop.
exercises.why: Single-leg glute strength directly supports hip stability at footstrike — a weak link here shows up as knee or IT band pain.

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Down
exercises.form_cue: Stand on a low step, slowly lower the opposite heel to tap the floor without letting your standing knee cave inward.
exercises.why: Trains the glute medius to control knee alignment on impact — this is the muscle behind most runner's-knee patterns.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.form_cue: Balance on one foot, rise onto the ball of your foot, full range, control the lowering.
exercises.why: Calf and Achilles strength on the exact single-leg pattern of push-off — the highest-value prehab for Achilles issues.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.form_cue: Hips stacked, don't let them sag. Modify on your knee if needed.
exercises.why: Lateral core strength that controls the side-to-side sway that creeps in as running fatigue sets in.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Heel down, toes up on a wall or step.
exercises.why: Releases what the calf raises just loaded.

progression_notes: Once single-leg glute bridges feel easy at 3x12, add a pause at the top. Increase single-leg calf raise reps before adding a weighted version.
